title: Cost of Meetings Calculator
description: Calculate the true financial impact of organization meetings based on participant salaries and duration.
methodSummary: Hourly salary allocation = average annual salary / 2,080.
Cost per meeting = participants × hourly allocation × duration in minutes / 60.
Annual allocation = cost per meeting × weekly frequency × 52.
assumptions: Based on 2080 working hours per year (40 hours/week).
Assumes all participants are focused 100% on the meeting for its duration.
Average salary is used for anonymity and speed.
insights: Eight participants at $90,000 for one hour each week allocate $18,000 of salary over 52 weeks.
Reducing that example to 30 minutes halves the allocation to $9,000; it does not automatically reduce payroll.

faqs.a: The model uses 40 paid hours × 52 weeks. It is a simple salary allocation assumption.

faqs.q: Does cancelling a meeting save cash?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Salaries usually continue; the time becomes available for other work.

richContent:
Compare a recurring meeting with an alternative

Eight participants earning an average $90,000 allocate $346.15 to a one-hour meeting. Over 52 weekly meetings that is $18,000. A 30-minute version allocates $9,000 annually. These are worked examples, not survey estimates.

Before changing the meeting, record its purpose, required participants and expected outcome. A costly meeting may be worthwhile if it prevents rework or resolves a decision. Compare time and outcomes together; this calculator cannot judge the value delivered.

What the estimate omits

Preparation and follow-up vary by person. Add those hours separately instead of applying an unexplained percentage. Paid holidays and cancelled meetings reduce the annual count below the 52-week assumption.
quickAnswer: This calculator allocates salary to meeting time. It does not measure meeting value, productivity, or the number of decisions made.
resultNote: Salary allocation is not automatically recoverable cash. Benefits, payroll taxes, preparation, room costs and follow-up are excluded.
